question: A Snellen acuity of 6/6 means the patient can read at 6 metres what a person with normal vision can read at 6 metres — it represents the minimum standard of normal acuity, not maximum visual capability.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. 6/6 is the minimum 'normal' by convention — it does not mean the best possible vision. Acuity better than 6/6 (e.g. 6/5 or 6/4) is commonly found in young healthy eyes and is well within the normal range.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Snellen notation is VA = test distance / distance at which a normal eye can just resolve that letter. 6/6 is the defined 'normal' threshold; many healthy young adults achieve 6/5 or better with full optical correction.
